tiers.t1: native edit (crop's own gene, NGT cat-1 candidate)

_schema.note: Gene/function/evidence are sourced facts. Portability tier, linkage, pleiotropy and IP are indicative research signals, not lab results or legal advice.

entries.name: Shoot sodium exclusion
entries.source: Wild wheat (Triticum monococcum, Nax2); rice OsHKT1;5 / SKC1
entries.does: Retrieves Na+ from the xylem so less reaches the shoot; keeps leaf Na+/K+ low under salinity.
entries.linkage: Native edit: no drag. Via wild-wheat introgression the Nax2 region first needed fine-mapping.
entries.pleiotropy: Strong Na+ exclusion usually well tolerated; very high K+ retrieval can trade off without salinity.

ip.text: HKT salt-tolerance applications have commercial history; run a patent query before use.

tomato.note: Tomato has SlHKT1;2; wild-tomato alleles track leaf Na+/K+ -> favourable native allele is an edit candidate.

wheat.note: Wheat's own story: Nax2 from crossable wild wheat.

rice.note: Rice OsHKT1;5 (SKC1) allele governs the trait.

entries.name: Plasma-membrane Na+ export
entries.does: Pumps Na+ out of the cell at the root surface and loads it for controlled long-distance handling.
entries.ref: Olias et al., 2009, Plant Cell Environ.
entries.linkage: Editing the crop's own gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: Dosage-sensitive: full knockout impairs growth under salt, so tune expression, do not remove.

ip.text: No specific patent confirmed in seed pass.

tomato.note: SlSOS1 is native and validated; tune its own expression/allele.

entries.name: Vacuolar sodium storage
entries.does: Moves Na+ into the vacuole; overexpression raises tolerance in several species.
entries.ref: Apse et al., 1999; later crop work
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: Constitutive overexpression can perturb K+ balance and growth; conditional expression safer.

ip.text: Long patent history across companies; confirm freedom-to-operate.

tomato.note: Native LeNHX family; edit the crop's own gene.

entries.name: Proton pump powering Na+ handling
entries.does: Vacuolar proton-pyrophosphatase; overexpression energises Na+ sequestration, improves salt/drought tolerance.
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: Highly pleiotropic: also affects auxin transport, root growth and P nutrition.

ip.text: AVP1 stress applications patented/licensed historically; verify before investing.

tomato.note: Native H+-PPase genes; up-regulate own copy.

entries.name: Whole-trait source: wild-tomato salt loci
entries.does: Mapped loci raise salt tolerance and fruit Na+/K+ balance; clearest salt-tolerance reservoir for cultivated tomato.
entries.linkage: HIGH linkage drag - the classic problem; salt loci often co-segregate with small fruit and poor quality. Fine-map + native edit to keep benefit without baggage.
entries.pleiotropy: Multi-gene loci; yield/fruit-size/quality effects common.

ip.text: Introgression lines may carry plant-breeders' rights; check registry.

tomato.note: Crossable with cultivated tomato - classic cisgenic/introgression route.

entries.name: Cytokinin-signalling brake (loss-of-function)
entries.does: A B-type response regulator in cytokinin signalling; knocking it out raises seedling salinity tolerance.
entries.linkage: Native loss-of-function edit of the crop's own gene -> no linkage drag. The textbook NGT-style salt edit.
entries.pleiotropy: Cytokinin signalling touches development; the knockout was tolerated in rice but wider effects should be checked per crop.

ip.text: CRISPR salt-tolerance edits are an active patent area; confirm freedom-to-operate.

rice.note: Rice's own gene, already edited successfully - the native route proven.

wheat.note: Cereal response-regulator orthologs exist; native-edit candidate, needs mapping.

tomato.note: Tomato has response regulators; an ortholog edit is a candidate but unproven in tomato.

entries.name: SOS-pathway activating kinase + a lost allele
entries.does: Activates the SOS Na+-export module; overexpression confers salt tolerance. A favourable promoter allele was partly LOST during tomato domestication, lowering salt resistance.
entries.ref: Huertas et al., 2012, Plant Cell Environ.; Wang et al., 2022, Hortic. Res.
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag. Restoring the lost promoter allele is a clean native edit.
entries.pleiotropy: SOS module is fairly salt-specific; kinase dosage still matters.

ip.text: No specific patent confirmed in seed pass.

tomato.note: Native SlSOS2; domestication thinned a favourable promoter allele -> restoring it is an NGT cat-1 candidate. A 'lost potential' case.

pepper.note: Native CIPK24 ortholog expected; native route.

entries.name: Master stress transcription factor
entries.does: A master regulator that switches on many downstream drought/salt genes at once; a constitutively active form raises tolerance.
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: Strong trade-off: constitutive activity stunts growth. Needs a stress-inducible promoter, not constitutive expression - HOW you edit matters as much as WHAT.

ip.text: DREB/CBF stress-tolerance patents are numerous across companies; verify freedom-to-operate.

tomato.note: Native SlDREB orthologs; edit for stress-inducible, not constitutive, activity.

entries.name: Protective LEA protein
entries.source: Rice OsLEA3-1; LEA family across plants
entries.does: A late-embryogenesis-abundant protein that shields cells under dehydration/salt; overexpression improved tolerance and field yield.
entries.ref: Xiao et al., 2007, Theor. Appl. Genet.
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: LEA proteins are protective with few reported growth penalties - relatively clean.

ip.text: LEA stress applications have patent history; confirm.

tomato.note: Native LEA family; up-regulate the crop's own protective genes.

entries.name: Thermotolerance QTL - clears heat-damaged proteins
entries.source: African rice (Oryza glaberrima); cultivated rice allele
entries.does: Encodes a 26S-proteasome subunit that clears heat-denatured proteins; a superior allele is a major thermotolerance QTL.
entries.evidence: Functional: QTL cloning, allele swap, field
entries.linkage: A natural superior allele within the rice gene pool - cisgenic introgression or native-allele edit; little drag if fine-mapped.
entries.pleiotropy: Proteasome housekeeping; the tolerant allele was carried in adapted rice without obvious penalty.

ip.text: Thermotolerance alleles can carry breeding IP; check.

rice.note: From African rice into cultivated rice - a documented allele route; or edit the native allele.

tomato.note: Proteasome subunits are conserved; a native-allele candidate, unproven in tomato.

entries.name: Heat-shock master switch
entries.does: A master heat-shock transcription factor; alternative splicing of HsfA2 drives the thermotolerance program in tomato.
entries.ref: Alternative splicing of HsfA2 mediates thermotolerance in tomato, 2017
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: HSF network is broad, but HsfA2 is stress-activated; generally tolerated.

ip.text: HSF thermotolerance applications exist; check.

tomato.note: Native SlHsfA2 - edit for a stronger stress-induced splice form.

entries.name: Drought NAC regulator (field-proven)
entries.does: A stress-responsive NAC transcription factor; overexpression improved drought resistance and raised field grain yield under drought, with little penalty.
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: Notably low yield penalty for a stress TF - a key reason it is attractive.

ip.text: NAC drought-yield applications are widely patented; verify freedom-to-operate.

rice.note: Rice's own SNAC1 - proven in field.

entries.name: Drought NAC silenced by a jumping gene
entries.does: A NAC factor whose promoter carries a transposon (MITE) insertion in many lines; the insertion silences the gene and lowers seedling drought tolerance - the favourable state is the TE-free allele.
entries.linkage: The favourable allele is native (TE-free) -> selecting or editing it carries no foreign drag. A 'lost by a jumping gene' case.
entries.pleiotropy: Seedling-stage drought; broader effects to check.

ip.text: Check patent activity on the allele/use.

maize.note: Maize's own gene - select the TE-free allele or edit to restore expression.

entries.name: Chilling-tolerance adaptation allele
entries.does: A G-protein-signalling regulator that senses cold; a japonica allele confers chilling tolerance that let rice spread to temperate climates.
entries.linkage: Favourable allele is native to rice -> native-allele edit/selection, no drag. A naturally selected adaptation allele.
entries.pleiotropy: G-protein signalling is broad; the cold allele was carried in adapted rice without obvious penalty.

ip.text: Check patent activity on the allele/use.

rice.note: The japonica adaptation allele - native to rice.

entries.name: Durable mildew resistance by removing a susceptibility gene
entries.source: Barley mlo; wheat TaMLO; tomato ol-2
entries.does: MLO is a gene powdery mildew needs to infect; knocking it out gives broad, durable resistance. Genome-edited in wheat without the usual growth penalty.
entries.ref: Li et al., 2022, Nature; barley mlo (classic)
entries.linkage: Loss-of-function edit of the crop's own gene -> no drag. The archetypal NGT S-gene edit.
entries.pleiotropy: mlo can carry minor leaf-spotting/yield cost; the 2022 wheat edit removed the penalty - manageable.

ip.text: S-gene editing for mildew resistance is actively patented; confirm freedom-to-operate.

wheat.note: Edited, no growth penalty - a landmark native edit.

grape.note: Native MLO; knockdown reduces mildew - candidate.

entries.name: Firmer fruit without blocking ripening
entries.does: Pectate lyase loosens the cell wall during softening; knocking it out makes fruit markedly firmer while colour, flavour and ripening proceed normally.
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag.
entries.pleiotropy: Knockout also reduced foliar pathogen susceptibility; unusually few downsides.

ip.text: Fruit-firmness edits are patented; confirm freedom-to-operate.

entries.name: Nitrogen-use-efficiency allele lost in one subspecies
entries.does: A nitrate transporter/sensor; the indica allele takes up and uses nitrate far better than the japonica allele - one natural variant with a large NUE effect.
entries.linkage: Favourable allele is native to rice -> native-allele swap/edit. The 'lost potential' case: japonica simply lacks the better allele.
entries.pleiotropy: Also shapes the root microbiome; broadly beneficial, watch context.

ip.text: NUE alleles can carry IP; check.

rice.note: Swap in the indica allele - native route, large effect.

entries.name: Acid-soil tolerance by organic-acid efflux
entries.source: Wheat TaALMT1 (malate); sorghum SbMATE (citrate); regulator STOP1
entries.does: Roots release organic acids that chelate toxic Al3+ in acid soils; superior alleles raise tolerance and root growth.
entries.ref: Sasaki et al., 2004 (TaALMT1); Magalhaes et al., 2007 (SbMATE)
entries.linkage: Native genes with superior natural alleles -> native-allele route; expression-level alleles matter.
entries.pleiotropy: Organic-acid efflux has a carbon cost but is generally well tolerated.

ip.text: Al-tolerance alleles have breeding IP; check.

wheat.note: TaALMT1 native allele - the documented case.

entries.name: Fruit-size regulator (domestication QTL)
entries.does: A negative regulator of cell division in the fruit; the large-fruit allele selected during domestication accounts for a big share of tomato fruit-size increase.
entries.linkage: Native gene with allelic variation -> native-allele route.
entries.pleiotropy: Fruit size trades off with fruit number; balance needed.

ip.text: Fruit-size alleles may carry IP; check.

tomato.note: Native fw2.2 allele - the classic size QTL.

entries.name: Florigen - the mobile flowering signal
entries.does: The florigen protein made in leaves that travels to the shoot tip to trigger flowering; tuning it shifts flowering time and adaptation to latitude/season.
entries.linkage: Native gene -> no drag; edit regulatory alleles to tune timing.
entries.pleiotropy: Flowering time strongly affects yield and adaptation - tune, don't switch on/off.

ip.text: FT/florigen applications patented; check.

entries.name: Grain number via a cytokinin brake
entries.does: A cytokinin-degrading enzyme in the inflorescence; a reduced-function allele keeps more cytokinin, making more grains per panicle.
entries.linkage: Native gene with dosage alleles -> native-allele/edit route.
entries.pleiotropy: Grain number can trade off with grain size; balance needed.

ip.text: Yield QTL alleles can carry IP; check.

entries.name: Seedlessness (stenospermocarpy)
entries.does: Master gene for seed/ovule development in fleshy fruits; suppression or knockout triggers seedlessness.
entries.ref: Royo et al. 2016; Florida A&M muscadine editing (USDA NIFA)
entries.linkage: Editing the crop's own AGL11 -> no drag, unlike crossing seedlessness in from another background.
entries.pleiotropy: AGL11/STK governs ovule and seed-coat development; loss can reduce berry size, firmness and fruit set.

ip.text: Concept published and actively pursued incl. public gene-editing projects for seedless grape. The case Burcu hit on blackberry: sound idea, taken space. Confirm freedom-to-operate first.

blackberry.note: Rubus carries its own AGL11; loss-of-function edit of the crop's own gene is the native route.

grape.note: Native VviAGL11 edit; most crowded IP space.

tomato.note: Tomato TAGL11 governs seed development; native-edit route, weigh fruit-set effects.
